summary: Arthur Maurice Hocart (1883–1939) was a scholar in archaeology and Indology who studied at Elizabeth College and Exeter College. He served as Archaeological Commissioner in Sri Lanka (1921–1929) and as Professor of Sociology at Cairo University (1934).
Arthur Philip McKeown works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), studying under Parimal G. Patil, Pari Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

Arthur Schopenhauer (1788–1860) was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin (under Schleiermacher, Boeckh, and Wolf), and Jena, receiving his doctorate in 1813. He attended lectures by Friedrich Majer and held a Dozentur at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1820.

Arthur Venis (1857–1918) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1885, 1888, 1897–1914) and Professor of Post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (1914–1918).

Arthur Waley (1889–1966) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at King's College, Cambridge, and under Gustav Haloun, Laurence Binyon, and Hidetsugu Yagi. He served at the British Museum (1913–1929) and SOAS (1948).

Arthur Wilhelm Gleye (1867–1937) was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Tartu (1888–1893) under Leo Meyer. He later served as Lecturer of German at Tomsk State University from 1901 to 1921.

Arthur William Ryder (1877–1938) was an Indologist educated at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig under Lanman, Geldner, and Windisch. He served as Assistant in Sanskrit at Harvard (1901–1906) and as Professor at the University of California (1906–1938).
Arthur Woollgar Verrall (1851–1912) was an academic who studied at Wellington College (~1865–1869) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1873). He also taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Arti Dhand (born 1966) specializes in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Calgary (~1988–1994) and McGill University (~1995–2000), and became Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto (~2002).

Artur Kibat (1878–1960) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Adalbert Bezzenberger and earned his PhD from the University of Königsberg (1898–1904), later working as a teacher at Oberrealschule Wilhelmshaven in 1910.
Aruna Haldar (born 1918) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose. She served as a teacher at Patna University.

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani (1921–2003) was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Mumbai under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He was professor and Sanskrit department head at MS University of Baroda (1967–1980) and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1975–1981).

Arvind Sharma (born 1940) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Queensland and University of Sydney, and was appointed to the Birks Chair at McGill in 1994.

Aryadeva (200–250) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nagarjuna and Shakyamitra. He was associated with the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning and taught disciples including Candrakīrti and Tilopa.
Aryendra Sharma was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Walther Wüst by 1939. He served as Director at Osmania University (attested 1969).

Asanga Tilakaratne (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Peradeniya and Hawaiʻi. He held chair and professorial posts at Kelaniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Colombo, where he became Emeritus Professor (~2017).
Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973). He later served as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin High School (attested 1978).

Aschwin Lippe (1914–1988) worked in Indology, Sinology, and archaeology, receiving his PhD from Humboldt University of Berlin (~1938–1942). He was an assistant and associate curator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1949–1973) and curator at the University of Paris (1980).

Asen Balikci (1929–2019) was a scholar in archaeology and related fields who earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1956. He worked at the National Museum of Canada (~1957–1963) and was a professor at the Université de Montréal (1963–1993).

Ashok Aklujkar (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy educated at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia from 1969 to 2006.
